headline: Ipswich and Forest share points after first-half goals

sentences.text: Ipswich Town and Nottingham Forest drew 1–1 in the Premier League at Portman Road, with both goals arriving before half-time.
Forest took the lead in the 13th minute when Neco Williams scored from Daniel Muñoz’s assist.
Ipswich levelled in the 41st minute through Julio Enciso, and the score remained unchanged after the interval.
The second half included a VAR review involving Ipswich’s Issa Diop, who was later booked, while Forest’s Murillo Santiago Costa dos Santos also received a yellow card.
Ipswich made 5 substitutions and Forest made 3 as both sides changed personnel during the game.
The possession split was nearly even, with Ipswich at 49.4% and Forest at 50.6%.
But Forest had the greater attacking volume, recording 17 shots to Ipswich’s 7 and 5 shots on target to 3.
The expected-goals figures also favoured Forest, at 2.29 to Ipswich’s 0.46, while Forest had 5 corners to none.
Ipswich completed 486 passes at 79% accuracy, compared with Forest’s 480 passes at 80%.
The draw extended Ipswich’s run of mixed results: they had collected 6 points from their previous 5 league matches, while Forest had taken 4 from their last 5.
Ipswich moved from 10th before kick-off to 9th, reaching 10 points after 8 matches.
Forest climbed from 19th to 16th and now have 6 points from 8 matches, with each side taking a point from the stalemate.
